title: Communication Theory

coding.name: Channel coding
coding.question: A channel makes errors or erasures. How much can a code repair, and how do we decode it?

signals.name: Signals and receivers
signals.question: How do bits become a waveform, and how does a receiver get them back out of the noise?

source.name: Source coding and limits
source.question: How few bits can describe a source, and how fast can a channel carry them?

references: R. G. Gallager, “Principles of Digital Communication”, Cambridge University Press, 2008
A. Lapidoth, “A Foundation in Digital Communication”, Cambridge University Press, 2009
T. M. Cover and J. A. Thomas, “Elements of Information Theory”, Wiley, 2nd edition, 2006
G. D. Forney, lecture notes of “Principles of Digital Communication II” (MIT 6.451), on which the channel coding part is based
further_reading: D. MacKay, “Information Theory, Inference, and Learning Algorithms”; J. Soni and R. Goodman, “A Mind at Play”; J. Gleick, “The Information”.
